technique_changes: DUPLICATE-RUN PROTOCOL: on finding a completed run for the same run_id, read that run's session line and decisions FIRST and re-derive only inputs that could have moved since its ts_end. Cost ~13 min instead of ~2h and produced two findings the full re-run would likely have reproduced identically, errors included. Worth making a standing rule: a second run's value is adversarial, not additive.

STATE-AGE DELTA, NOT JUST AGE: S-20260915-01 logged state_age_h 22.1 and proceeded. The useful quantity was not the age but the fact that a refresh landed 20 minutes after it finished. Recommend runs record state generated_at and compare against the PRIOR run's, so a refresh between runs is visible as a reason to re-check rather than something to discover by accident.

NATIONAL OWNERSHIP IS NOT CONTESTEDNESS: preflight's CONTESTED heuristic keys on pct_owned, which is national. In a 10-team league where every roster is 16/16, the binding constraint is whether a rival must cut a real player, and which specific rival has a motive. Both of this week's claim calls invert under the in-league test. Recommend preflight take roster-room and a named-rival motive as inputs rather than branching on pct_owned alone.

PROMPT AS A SOURCE OF ERROR: two of this run's findings (the D/ST rule, the 'start at 001' instruction) are errors in the routine prompt itself, not in the analysis. Runs should treat standing instructions as claims to be checked against outcomes, the same as any projection. The 12-hour rule, bye caps and never-submit rules are NOT in this category and were followed exactly.

technique_changes: STATE FRESHNESS: computed state_age_h (22.1h) before reasoning and stated it in the first push line, per the FIX-PLAN's proposed gate. SCORING VERIFICATION: first run to test a config rule against actual scored data instead of inheriting it. This found the D/ST error. Generalises: the first scored week is the only chance to verify every scoring claim in config.json cheaply, and no prior run took it.

STATE FILE HANDLING: curled the state file to disk and queried it with Python rather than reading it into context. Full fidelity, ~2k tokens instead of ~30k, and it made the 10-roster trade scan and the position-cap table mechanical.

PRE-FLIGHT SCOPE: ran check_move() on 16 moves including five deliberately illegal shapes, to document WHY they are illegal in the log rather than asserting it in prose. CLAIM ECONOMICS INVERTED: at waiver #10 a successful claim costs nothing, so the Sep 8 rule ('spend priority only on contested players') stops binding. This run claims the best contested player available and treats the uncontested ones as Wednesday free adds. Worth testing whether the framework should carry waiver position as an explicit input rather than a note.
